record.category: open source relational database server (software the user installs and runs)

free_tier.stated: MariaDB Server is a general purpose open source relational database management system; released under the GPLv2 open source licence and guaranteed to remain open source
free_tier.notes: No hosted quota applies: the software is downloaded and run by the user. Packages are available in the standard repositories of all major Linux distributions and from the MariaDB Foundation download site.

per_object_cap.stated: unverified: no per-object or total size cap stated on the first-party pages read; capacity is set by the machine the user runs the server on
per_object_cap.notes: This is self-hosted software, so any cap is a property of the user's machine, not of the offer.

retention.stated: unverified: no retention limit stated on the first-party pages read; data persists on the user's own storage until deleted
retention.notes: Retention is determined by the user's own storage and backups, not by the vendor.

egress.terms: no egress charge or quota applies; the server runs on the user's own machine and network

record.interface_detail: the MySQL/MariaDB wire protocol over TCP with the mariadb command-line client and connectors for C, Java, ODBC, Python and Node.js; the protocol token has no dedicated interface term in the vocabulary
record.tooling: the user installs and runs the mariadb-server package or binary on a rented or free machine; connectors exist for C, Java, ODBC, Python and Node.js, and Galera clustering and a Kubernetes operator are available; rclone does not apply
record.chaining: a MariaDB Server instance the user installs and runs on a rented or free machine is the self-hosted option of last resort; hosted managed databases such as MariaDB Cloud (MariaDB plc) are separate offers and come first whenever a hosted tier is available

limits.value: max_connections defaults to 151, configurable by the user via an option file or SET GLOBAL

record.binding_note: This is self-hosted software with no vendor-imposed quota; the only stated configurable limit is max_connections, which the user can raise, so no corpus limit binds the offer itself.

identity_cost.detail: the MariaDB Server download page offers packages and repository setup with no account, card or sign-in; the newsletter email field on that page is an optional subscription, not a download gate

record.reliability_note: LTS releases are maintained for three years; the software is self-operated, so availability and backups depend on the user's own machine.
record.confidence_note: First-party pages read on 2026-11-19: mariadb.org/en, mariadb.org/download, mariadb.org/about and the MariaDB Community Server docs.

evidence.quote: MariaDB Server is released under the GPLv2 open source licence and is guaranteed to remain open source.
evidence.proved: the server is open source under GPLv2 with no licence fee

evidence.quote: MariaDB Server is a general purpose open source relational database management system.
MariaDB Foundation provides packages for MariaDB versions newer than the version provided by the distribution only.
evidence.proved: the Foundation provides downloadable packages with no account gate on the download page

evidence.quote: Server behavior lives in system variables, such as the `max_connections` variable, which caps how many clients can connect at once. Its default is 151
evidence.proved: the default client connection cap and that it is a user-configurable server setting

record.notes: The MariaDB Foundation stewards the open source MariaDB Server; it is not a hosted provider. What it offers is software the user installs and runs, so this is the self-hosted option of last resort, recorded behind every hosted database in the topic. MariaDB Cloud is a separate managed offer from MariaDB plc and is not what this record describes. The only quota found on a first-party page is the configurable max_connections default of 151.
